_comment: Lane definitions for suno-forge. Descriptor pools are ordered by priority: earlier items are more characteristic and are selected more often. Real artist names NEVER appear here (not even in labels); the artist-to-lane mapping lives only in README.md and research/.

connor-price.label: Bouncy playful trap-pop
connor-price.description: Bouncy, playful trap-pop instrumental: tight syncopated drums, bright synth plucks and bells, stop-start arrangement with mutes and drops, crisp clean modern mix.

bpm.note: Written half-time trap count (felt 65-80). Analysed tracks in this lane sit at 130-141 half-time or 100-112 straight-time; use --bpm 105 for the straight bounce (the planner switches to straight time under 120).

model.rationale: Needs crisp transient detail, clean stereo plucks and tight drum programming; the flagship model has the cleanest mix and follows stop-start structure cues best.
model.wild: Try the experimental/wild variant when the result is too generic pop and you want odd fills, unexpected synth timbres or playful rhythmic turnarounds.

sliders.weirdnessWhy: Low-moderate: keep the drums tight and the hook predictable; raise only if the plucks feel stock.
sliders.styleInfluenceWhy: High: the Style field carries the whole identity (bounce, plucks, stop-start) and must be followed closely.

drums: crisp rolling hi-hats with triplet stutters
bass: bouncy sub bass that follows the kick

intro: finger snaps and a filtered hi-hat
hook: catchy whistle-like lead doubles the plucks
hook_final: drums cut for the last beat then slam back
verse: kick and snare only with sparse plucks
verse_mutes: full stop on the last beat of every 4th bar
beat drops out for one bar then returns
plucks and drums trade short phrases
break: one bar of silence before the drop
drop: snare on every 2 and 4 with rimshot layers
switch: tempo feel flips to straight time
outro_hard-stop: everything stops together on the downbeat

listenFor: Does the beat actually stop and restart on the mute bars, or does Suno smooth them over? If smoothed, lead the drums group with 'stop-start drum mutes' and put 'full stop' cues in more sections.
Plucks should be bright and forward; if they are buried, make 'bright synth plucks' the first instrument descriptor.
Hi-hats should bounce and stutter, not run as a flat 16th grid; if rigid, add 'swung 16th hi-hats' and raise Weirdness by 10.
Suno likes to add sung hooks or ad-libs on bouncy pop beats; if any appear, add 'singing, pop vocals' to the Exclude field and re-roll.

paak-pocket.label: Live swung neo-soul funk hip hop
paak-pocket.description: Live-drummer neo-soul/funk hip hop instrumental: swung drums played behind the beat, Rhodes and Wurlitzer chords, fingered bass guitar, breakbeat feel, warm analog saturation.

bpm.note: Straight-time, swung 16ths. Sweet spot 86-96; 98-105 leans funk; 78-86 leans lo-fi soul.

model.rationale: Live-sounding drums and real-instrument timbres (Rhodes, bass guitar, horns) need the most realistic acoustic rendering and the loosest timing feel; the flagship model renders swing and room most convincingly.
model.wild: Try the experimental/wild variant when the groove comes back too clean and quantized, or you want odd meters, drunken fills and tape-warped chords.

sliders.weirdnessWhy: Mid: enough looseness to humanize the drums and chord voicings without derailing the groove; the pocket comes from the vocabulary, not the slider.
sliders.styleInfluenceWhy: Moderate-high: follow the instrument list closely but let the model improvise the pocket.

drums: live drum kit played behind the beat
tight dry snare with a light brushed touch

safer: live drum kit played behind the beat

hook_final: bass walks up into the final chord
verse: drums simplify to kick snare and shuffled hats
verse_mutes: bass and Rhodes carry one bar alone
break: live kit solo with ghost notes
switch: drummer moves to a breakbeat pattern
outro: band thins to drums and bass

listenFor: The kick and snare should feel pulled back behind the grid; if the drums sound like a drum machine, lead the drums group with 'live drum kit played behind the beat' and add 'drunk swing', then raise Weirdness to 50-55.
Rhodes should sound like an electric piano, not a synth pad; if it is pad-like, add 'Wurlitzer' and 'clavinet stabs' and remove any pad words.
Bass should be fingered guitar, not an 808; if it is a sub, add '808 trap bass' to Exclude (it is in the lane preset) and 'muted palm bass' to Style.
Suno likes to add hummed or sung melodies on soul grooves; if one appears, add 'singing, scat' to Exclude and re-roll.

jid-dark.label: Dense dark boom-bap/trap hybrid
jid-dark.description: Dense, dark boom-bap/trap hybrid instrumental: pitched chopped sample textures, odd drum fills and switch-ups, busy hi-hats with rapid triplet rolls, cinematic strings and choir pads.

bpm.note: Written half-time trap tempo (felt 70-80). For a boom-bap-first feel use --bpm 90 which switches to straight time.

model.rationale: Dense layered arrangements, sample-chop textures and beat switches need the model with the best structural adherence and the clearest low-mid separation so strings, chops and 808 do not blur.
model.wild: Try the experimental/wild variant for odd fills, unexpected time-feel changes and stranger chop textures; this lane benefits most from the wild variant.

sliders.weirdnessWhy: Moderate-high: odd fills, off-kilter chops and switch-ups are the point of this lane; stay under 60 so the beat switch stays on plan.
sliders.styleInfluenceWhy: Moderate-high: the Style field defines the hybrid; too low and it collapses into generic trap.

genre: gritty East Coast meets Southern trap
drums: busy hi-hats with rapid triplet rolls
heavy boom-bap snare over trap hats
hard knocking boom-bap kick and snare
mix: wide stereo pads with centered drums

safer: busy hi-hats with rapid triplet rolls

hook_final: sub drop into the last bar
verse: kick and snare knock with sparse hats
verse_mutes: drums stop on the last bar of each 8
chop plays alone for one bar
drums return with a snare rush
switch: tempo feel flips to straight boom bap
drums cut for two bars then new pattern slams in
key shifts up a minor third
hook_part-b: boom-bap drums with trap hats layered

listenFor: The chop should sound like a pitched, sliced sample, not a sung lead; if Suno renders it as a vocal melody, swap the sample descriptor for 'detuned piano chops' and add 'vocal melody' to Exclude.
Hi-hats should be busy with rolls and pattern switches; if flat, add 'snare rushes' to Style and 'hi-hats switch pattern at bar 9' cues to the verses.
The beat switch should be audible as a real pattern change; if not, make the switch section 8 bars and keep 'beat switch halfway' in the Style field.
Strings can take over and turn it into a trailer cue; if they do, add 'cinematic trailer, epic orchestra' to Exclude and keep strings behind the drums in cue ordering.

phonk-experimental.label: Memphis-rooted original phonk
phonk-experimental.description: Original/experimental phonk instrumental: Memphis-style cowbell patterns, distorted saturated 808s, tape hiss and vinyl crackle, chopped-and-screwed sample textures used as instruments, lo-fi jazz/soul samples, off-grid swing, dark minor keys. Not drift phonk.

bpm.note: Written 130-150 half-time (felt 65-75). Classic SoundCloud phonk sits at 130-140; slower feels more screwed.

model.rationale: Lo-fi grit, tape hiss and chopped textures are easy to render but the model must hold the swing and keep the cowbell audible in a distorted mix; the flagship model handles this with the best control.
model.wild: Try the experimental/wild variant often here: this lane thrives on off-grid drums, stranger chops and tape-warped pitch, which the wild variant leans into.

sliders.weirdnessWhy: Upper end of the usable hip hop range: off-grid swing, screwed textures and grit are the goal, but above 60 Suno starts drifting tempo and structure.
sliders.styleInfluenceWhy: Moderate: hold the Memphis palette but let the model get experimental with chops and texture.

drums: dusty drum machine kick and snare
harmony: chopped and screwed sample textures used as instruments
mix: murky low-passed mix with a controlled clean sub

hook: Memphis cowbell pattern rides the off-beats
hook_final: drums cut for the last beat then slam back
verse: cowbell drops to a sparse pattern
snare hits only every other bar
verse_mutes: full stop on the last beat of every 4th bar
bridge: slowed sample and tape hiss only
break_drums-only: one bar of tape hiss silence

listenFor: Cowbell should be a rhythmic pattern in the drums, not a lead melody; a cowbell melody means it drifted into drift phonk. Add 'cowbell lead melody' to Exclude and lead the drums group with 'Memphis cowbell pattern'.
The 808 should be distorted and saturated but still readable; if it is a clean sine sub, make 'blown-out sub bass' the bass descriptor.
Chopped textures should read as sliced, slowed samples; if Suno sings actual words, add 'lyrics, vocal melody' to Exclude and swap the sample-texture descriptor for 'eerie detuned keys'.
Drums should feel dragged and off-grid; if they are rigid, add 'unquantized drum machine feel' to Style and raise Weirdness by 5-10 (stay under 60).

hybrid.label: Phonk drums + neo-soul pocket + trap-pop brightness
hybrid.description: Hybrid instrumental: Memphis-style cowbell and distorted 808 drums with off-grid swing, under live-feel neo-soul Rhodes chords and fingered bass pocket, topped with bright synth plucks and a clean punchy stop-start arrangement.

bpm.note: Written half-time so the phonk drums read correctly (felt 68-75); the Rhodes/bass pocket sits on the felt pulse.

model.rationale: Genre blends need the model with the best multi-genre coherence so the lo-fi drums, warm Rhodes and bright plucks share one mix instead of switching genres mid-song.
model.wild: Try the experimental/wild variant when the blend comes back as three songs stitched together; the wild variant tends to fuse unusual combinations more organically.

sliders.weirdnessWhy: Mid-high: a three-way blend needs some freedom to fuse, but not so much that it drifts into a fourth genre.
sliders.styleInfluenceWhy: Moderate-high: keep the specified instruments but allow re-balancing between them.

genre: lo-fi Memphis drums with live funk pocket
drums: off-grid swung kick and snare behind the beat
dusty drum machine with live-drummer swing
bass: distorted 808 under a fingered bass guitar
harmony: major 7th chord stabs over a minor bass
mix: clean punchy master with lo-fi drum texture

safer: off-grid swung kick and snare behind the beat
distorted 808 under a fingered bass guitar
clean punchy master with lo-fi drum texture

intro: Rhodes chord loop with tape hiss
bright pluck motif answers the chords
hook: distorted 808 and Memphis cowbell slam in
kick and snare behind the beat
hook_final: drums cut for the last beat then slam back
verse: Rhodes and bass carry the pocket
verse_part-b: beat flips to straight-time live funk feel
a swung live-feel kit replaces the drum machine
cowbell drops to a sparse pattern
verse_mutes: full stop on the last beat of every 4th bar
switch: tempo feel flips to straight-time funk
hook_part-b: live-feel swung drums with cowbell layered

listenFor: All three elements must coexist in one mix: lo-fi cowbell drums, warm Rhodes and bass, bright plucks. If Suno picks one genre and drops the others, raise Weirdness to 55-60 and reorder Style to lead with the missing element.
The drums should swing behind the beat; a rigid cowbell grid means it drifted toward drift phonk. Add 'quantized rigid drums, cowbell lead melody' to Exclude if either shows up.
Plucks should sit on top and stay bright; if they are dull, add 'sparkly bell lead' and 'bright top end' near the end of Style.
Suno may add hummed soul melodies on Rhodes grooves; if one appears, add 'singing, scat' to Exclude and re-roll.
